@.claude/backlog/039-agent-git-guard-wrapper-bypass.md can you implement this? handoff: # Handoff — backlog 039, agent Git guard wrapper bypass

**Written:** 2026-07-30
**Repo:** AHKFlowApp (`C:\Dev\segocom-github\AHKFlowApp`)
**Focus for the next session:** pick up `.claude/backlog/039-agent-git-guard-wrapper-bypass.md`.

Read the backlog item first. It holds the reproduction table, acceptance criteria, scope
boundaries, and the known traps. This document does **not** repeat them. It covers only what the
file cannot tell you: why it exists, what was already settled, and where the real risk sits.

---

## Why 039 was created

It was not planned work. It came out of a failed verification attempt at the very end of PR #235.

PR #235 rescoped the agent Git guard from "block every mutation in the main checkout" to a
three-tier model (always-allow / prompt / hard-deny). Merged as `0e20c8ec`. Its own final review
raised one thing tests could not close: **nothing had ever confirmed that a `Tier 1a` decision
actually renders as a visible permission prompt.** Every piece of `Ask` evidence was the JSON
contract asserted in process. So the plan carried two manual checks as the last gate before merge.

Trying to run those checks produced three findings, in order:

1. **The checks could not test the branch at all.** The guard hook resolves its script paths from
   the project directory, so a session rooted in the main checkout runs *main's* copy of the guard.
   At that point main was still the pre-merge commit — the old code. The user caught this. The first
   attempt (`git worktree prune` from main) had run silently, which the *old* guard should have
   hard-denied. That anomaly is what started the investigation.

2. **The wrapper bypass** — the actual subject of 039. See the backlog item for the measured table.
   The one-line version: the guard identifies a git invocation from each command segment's leading
   word, a user-level hook rewrites `git …` into `rtk git …`, so that word is `rtk` and no git
   invocation is found.

3. **One observation that is still unexplained.** A path-qualified probe that the wrapper's matcher
   should not rewrite *also* went unblocked, even though both guard copies classify it as blocking
   when called in process. Recorded in 039 under Notes.

The item was filed rather than fixed inline for two reasons. It predates PR #235 and affects the old
guard identically, so it is not that PR's regression to fix. And the fix is a design decision
(teach the guard to see through a wrapper prefix, or take `git` out of the rewrite), not a patch.
The user explicitly chose to park it.

## What is already settled — do not reopen

- **The tier model and every tier boundary.** Settled by PR #235 across three tasks, six review
  rounds, and a whole-branch review. `docs/agents/cross-agent-git-guardrails.md` on main is the
  current reference.
- **`git commit` is a permanent hard denial, never a prompt.** A `PreToolUse` approval cannot reach
  the `.githooks/pre-commit` backstop, so an approved prompt would still die there. Reasoning is in
  the guardrails doc and in the merged plan.
- **`AHKFLOW_ALLOW_MAIN=1` keeps its original meaning for every tier, including `commit`.** This was
  resolved directly with the user mid-plan; the plan document alone is ambiguous on it.
- **File edits in main are unguarded.** Known, accepted, separate limitation.

## The real risk in this work

Finding 3 above. If the guard's decision is not reaching the harness for reasons *beyond* the
wrapper rewrite, then fixing the wrapper alone will look correct in unit tests and still leave the
guard inert in practice. Treat "prove a real prompt appears end to end" as the exit criterion, not
"the wrapped form now returns Deny in process".

Suggested order:

1. Reproduce both the wrapper bypass and the unexplained path-qualified case, in that order.
2. Settle whether they share a root cause before choosing a fix.
3. Only then implement, with the regression tests 039 asks for.
4. Finish by doing what PR #235 never could: confirm a live `Ask` prompt renders.

## Technique that made this measurable

Classification can be read directly, with no git command executed and nothing mutated — this is
how the 039 table was produced, and it is the fastest loop for this task:

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -Command "
. ./scripts/agents/agent-worktree-guard.common.ps1
`$main = 'C:/Dev/segocom-github/AHKFlowApp'
foreach (`$cmd in @('git commit -m x','rtk git commit -m x')) {
  `$d = Invoke-AgentGuardPolicy -Command `$cmd -Cwd `$main -ProtectedRepoRoot `$main
  '{0,-28} => {1,-6} {2}' -f `$cmd, `$d.Action, `$d.Rule
}"
```

Useful property: this bypasses the hook plumbing entirely, so it separates "the policy decided
wrong" from "the decision never arrived" — precisely the distinction finding 3 turns on.

## Environment state you will inherit

- `main` is at `0e20c8ec`, clean, and carries the new guard plus the 039 file.
- Guard suites on main: `tests/AgentWorktreeGuard.Tests.ps1` 301 cases,
  `tests/AgentPreCommitHook.Tests.ps1` 11. Both green at merge.
- **Cleanup left unfinished.** The worktree `.claude/worktrees/fix-wt-agent-git-guard-scope` and its
  local branch still exist. Removal failed with `Permission denied` — the previous Claude session
  held a lock on the folder, and both detached watchers timed out. The exact commands to finish it
  are in `.claude/worktrees/worktree-removal.log` (tail of file). Its per-worktree database and
  Docker Compose project were also not reclaimed; `scripts/prune-worktree-databases.ps1` and
  `scripts/prune-worktree-docker.ps1` handle that.
- Codex needs a session restart to pick up the republished worktrees skill from PR #235.

## Working-agreement notes carried forward

- Create the worktree **before** writing any plan, and commit plans from the main checkout under
  `docs/superpowers/` (separate private repo). See `.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
- Ask questions in normal text while continuing to work. Do not present a blocking menu for routine
  choices or for "what next" — pick one, say which, keep going. (This was gotten wrong in the
  previous session.)
- Commit messages: extremely concise, grammar optional. Prose and docs: Plain English per
  `AGENTS.md`.

## Suggested skills

- **`superpowers:systematic-debugging`** — invoke first. This is a "why did the guard not fire"
  investigation with one confirmed cause and one unexplained observation; that is exactly the shape
  this skill is for. Do not start editing the guard before it.
- **`superpowers:brainstorming`** — the fix is a design choice with a security boundary
  (prefix-skipping must not let a wrapper *escalate* permissions). Settle the approach before code.
- **`mp-grilling`** — worth using on the chosen approach specifically. A wrapper allow-list is the
  kind of decision that looks obvious and has a sharp edge.
- **`worktrees`** — for the isolated workspace, and for the stale-worktree cleanup noted above.
- **`superpowers:test-driven-development`** — 039's acceptance criteria are already written as
  assertions (wrapped Tier 2 allow, wrapped Tier 1a Ask, wrapped Tier 1b deny).
- **`dck-verify`** — before any PR.
- Skip `dck-blazor-mudblazor`, `dck-ef-core`, and the other application-layer skills. This work
  touches only PowerShell guard scripts, their tests, and docs.

## References

- Backlog item: `.claude/backlog/039-agent-git-guard-wrapper-bypass.md`
- Merged PR (context, review history, and the full bypass writeup in its comments):
  <https://github.com/s205109/AHKFlowApp/pull/235>
- Guard implementation: `scripts/agents/agent-worktree-guard.common.ps1`
  (`Test-AgentGitTier2Allowed`, `Get-AgentGitLocationDecision`, `ConvertFrom-AgentHookInput`)
- Adapter: `scripts/agents/invoke-agent-worktree-guard.ps1`
- Bash shim: `.claude/hooks/pre-bash-guard.sh`
- Reference doc: `docs/agents/cross-agent-git-guardrails.md`
- Backstop: `.githooks/pre-commit.ps1`
- Wrapper hook registration: `PreToolUse` entry in the user-level `~/.claude/settings.json`
  (outside this repo, unversioned)

Session isolation is a property of the session, fixed when it starts. This session started in the worktree. Switching path mid-session — cd, absolute path, resolved path — does not move that boundary.

And the path already resolves to main. docs/superpowers in the worktree is a symlink:

superpowers -> /c/Dev/segocom-github/AHKFlowApp/docs/superpowers

So every way of naming that file lands on the same real file in the main checkout. The guard resolves it and refuses. Edit said so directly: "This session is isolated in the worktree ... Edit the worktree copy of this file instead of the shared-checkout path."

Extra catch: there is no worktree copy to fall back to. The public repo gitignores docs/superpowers, so git worktree add never checks it out. new-worktree.ps1 links the main folder in instead. The error's suggested fallback does not exist for this path.

What would have worked: starting a session in the main checkout. Then no worktree isolation, and CLAUDE.md's rule is satisfied too — plan writes and plan commits belong in main.

One honest limit: I only ever had Edit refused on that path. I never tried a plain Bash write to it, so I cannot say from evidence whether Bash would refuse the same way. The session-level reasoning says it should, but I did not test it. can you test it using bash first?
